prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
The tab was already closed; the browser is shut down. Work is complete.

[goal] Rebuild Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" as a low-poly 3D wallpaper in a single code-built HTML file, plus result.json.

[action] Identified the print visually (./print.jpg): the Great Wave curling from the left, three funaya, Mount Fuji small centre-right, clouds upper right, Prussian-blue/cream palette. Built ./scene/index.html with Three.js r170 from CDN: rounded low-poly swells with white foam puffs, a torus curl on the great wave, three ochre boats with crew and oars, cone Fuji with snow cap and zigzag snowline, cloud puffs, rippled water plane; gentle motion (wave bob, foam drift, boat bob/roll, cloud drift, camera sway). Wrote ./result.json. Verified by opening the file in a browser — renders correctly.

[result]
- ./scene/index.html — single file, no build step, only dependency is https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js (import map).
- ./result.json — records: boats = 3 (one under the great wave left, one central trough, one right swell); mountain = Mount Fuji (Fuji-san); plus composition, palette hexes, motion, assumptions.
- Verified: browser screenshot shows the great wave with curl on the left, three boats, Fuji, clouds, cream sky — recognizable at a glance.

[found / how I know it is right] The print is Hokusai's Kanagawa oki nami ura (Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, c. 1831, public domain): the title cartouche is visible top-left in the image, and the composition (wave left, three boats, small snow-capped Fuji centre-right) matches the known print. Boat count (3) read directly from the image. Scene verified live in the browser.

[assumptions] Low poly = flat-shaded primitives; "gentle motion" = slow bobbing/drift; the print is reference only, no texture loaded; camera fixed with subtle sway.

[limits] The curl is a torus arc (stylized), not the print's exact claw foam; Fuji is a small stylized cone. Both are intentional low-poly interpretations.
